title: Part 43: Aircraft Maintenance
description: Learn maintenance requirements, inspections, preventive maintenance, and airworthiness from 14 CFR Part 43

questions.question: What is the maximum interval for an annual inspection?
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.409, an annual inspection is required every 12 calendar months.

questions.question: When is a 100-hour inspection required?
options: For aircraft used for hire or flight instruction
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.409, a 100-hour inspection is required for aircraft carrying passengers for hire or providing flight instruction for hire.

questions.question: How much can the 100-hour inspection interval be exceeded to reach a place of inspection?
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.409, the 100-hour limit may be exceeded by up to 10 hours to reach a place where the inspection can be done, but the excess must be included in the next 100-hour interval.

questions.question: Who may perform an annual inspection?
options: A&P with IA or appropriately rated repair station
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 43.3 and 43.7, annual inspections may only be performed by an A&P mechanic with Inspection Authorization (IA) or an appropriately rated repair station.

questions.question: Who may perform a 100-hour inspection?
options: Any A&P mechanic or appropriately rated repair station
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 43.3, a 100-hour inspection may be performed by any certificated A&P mechanic or appropriately rated repair station.

questions.question: What preventive maintenance may a private pilot perform on an aircraft they own or operate?
options: Any maintenance they feel qualified to do
Specific items listed in Part 43 Appendix A
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 43.3(g), a certificated pilot may perform preventive maintenance on an aircraft owned or operated by that pilot, limited to items in Appendix A.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered preventive maintenance a pilot may perform?
questions.explanation: Per Part 43 Appendix A, replenishing hydraulic fluid is preventive maintenance. Replacing brake pads and adjusting cables require an A&P.

questions.question: What must be done after preventive maintenance is performed?
options: Have an A&P sign off the work
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 43.9, the person performing preventive maintenance must make an entry in the maintenance records describing the work performed.

questions.question: What is an Airworthiness Directive (AD)?
options: A legally enforceable rule requiring corrective action
questions.explanation: An AD is a legally enforceable rule issued by the FAA when an unsafe condition exists in a product and is likely to exist in other products of the same design.

questions.question: Who is responsible for ensuring compliance with Airworthiness Directives?
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.403, the owner or operator is primarily responsible for maintaining the aircraft in an airworthy condition, including compliance with ADs.

questions.question: What records must be kept for an aircraft?
options: Only the most recent annual inspection
Maintenance records, 100-hour/annual inspections, AD compliance, major alterations
Only records from the past 5 years
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.417, records must be kept for maintenance, inspections, AD compliance, and major alterations/repairs.

questions.question: How long must maintenance records be retained?
options: Until work is superseded or for 1 year after work performed
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.417, maintenance records must be retained until the work is repeated or superseded, or for 1 year after the work is performed.

questions.question: What must a maintenance record entry include?
options: Description of work, date, signature, and certificate number
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 43.9, entries must include description of work, date completed, signature, certificate number, and certificate type.

questions.question: What is a major repair?
options: A repair that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, or other qualities affecting airworthiness
Any repair requiring more than 8 hours
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 43.2, a major repair is one that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness.

questions.question: After a major repair, what is required before returning the aircraft to service?
options: Approval for return to service by authorized person and FAA Form 337
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 43.9 and 43.5, major repairs require approval for return to service by an authorized person and completion of FAA Form 337.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a progressive inspection program?
options: To spread inspection requirements over time for aircraft in continuous service
To allow pilots to do their own inspections
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.409(d), a progressive inspection program spreads the inspection requirements over time, useful for aircraft in continuous service.

questions.question: What does 'return to service' mean?
options: The aircraft is approved as airworthy after maintenance
The aircraft completes a test flight
questions.explanation: Return to service means the aircraft has been approved as airworthy after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration.

questions.question: Who may approve an aircraft for return to service after an annual inspection?
options: Only an IA holder or appropriately rated repair station
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 43.7, only an A&P with IA or an appropriately rated repair station may approve return to service after an annual inspection.

questions.question: What is required for an aircraft to be considered airworthy?
options: Conformity to type certificate and safe operating condition
questions.explanation: An aircraft is airworthy when it conforms to its type certificate (or approved alterations) and is in a condition for safe operation.

questions.question: Which of these is preventive maintenance a pilot may perform?
questions.explanation: Per Part 43 Appendix A, replacing landing gear tires is preventive maintenance. Spark plug replacement and magneto timing require an A&P.

questions.question: What is the ELT battery replacement interval?
options: When 50% of useful life expires or after 1 hour cumulative use
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.207, ELT batteries must be replaced when 50% of useful life has expired or after 1 hour of cumulative use.

questions.question: How often must a transponder be inspected?
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.413, transponders must be inspected every 24 calendar months.

questions.question: How often must a static system and altimeter be inspected for IFR flight?
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 91.411, the altimeter and static system must be inspected every 24 calendar months for IFR operations.

questions.question: What documents must be on board the aircraft for flight?
options: ARROW: Airworthiness certificate, Registration, Radio license (international), Operating limitations, Weight and balance
questions.explanation: ARROW documents must be on board: Airworthiness certificate, Registration, Radio station license (if international), Operating limitations (POH), Weight and balance data.

questions.question: What is a Special Flight Permit (ferry permit)?
options: Permission to fly in special use airspace
Authorization to fly an aircraft that doesn't meet airworthiness requirements for a specific purpose
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 21.197, a Special Flight Permit allows operation of an aircraft that doesn't currently meet airworthiness requirements for purposes like flying to a repair facility.
